uncited: It builds on [Delaunay Cover Refinement](13422-delaunay-cover-refinement.md) by adding a termination condition based on domain coverage rather than just local feature size satisfaction.
*   Optional parameter $r$: A positive number such that any connected component contains at least one ball of radius $r$.
**Probing Loop:** Continuously probe the domain $\Omega$ to find points.
*   *Alternative Initialization:* Attempt to form a large triangle first, then refine and check if the component is meshed.
**Termination Check:** The algorithm terminates when the domain is covered with probed Voronoi cells.
*   **Proof Sketch:** If the algorithm ends, the domain is covered with probed Voronoi cells (distance $\le \varepsilon$).
Each connected component includes a ball of radius $\ge \varepsilon$.
Thus, a probed segment intersects this ball (creating a probed point inside the volume).
There also exists an infinite Voronoi edge providing a point outside the volume (clipped on the boundary of $\Omega$).
Since the set of probes is connected and the surface is closed, a probed segment must intersect the surface.
If this intersection point was not added to the triangulation, it would be at distance $< \varepsilon$ from a mesh face, and thus at most $2\varepsilon$ from a meshed component.
*   **Initialization Efficiency:** Initializing all isolated points at once is faster than one-by-one, as it initializes several components simultaneously, reducing refinement steps.
*   **Time Complexity:** The cost is proportional to the volume of the bounding volume $\Omega$.
*   At least 80% of components are meshed on average in the partial implementation (isolated points only).
*   Use when the surface geometry is unknown and no seed points are available.
*   Use when the surface consists of multiple disconnected components, some of which may be small or isolated.
Implemented as a partial version including only the treatment of isolated points.
The mesh is initialized and refined while isolated points exist.
